candidates.name: Scalable structure-aware fusion planning
candidates.rationale: Joint topological scheduling, specialization, fusion, and construction-amortization optimization; extends previously solved tiny exact-scheduling repairs without requiring an optimum.

candidates.name: Inverse compact unitary compilation
candidates.rationale: Dense public operators hide compact generating circuits; mixed discrete topology and continuous angles, with private feasibility certificates.

candidates.name: Budgeted active coherent-noise calibration
candidates.rationale: Shot-limited adaptive experiment design must resolve aliasing and nuisance parameters across held-out noise families.

candidates.name: Parametric-fusion semantic counterexample
candidates.rationale: Official PR720 supplies a tiny sandwich failure; too readily reduced to a minimal standard regression case.

candidates.name: MPI FusedSWAP workspace repair
candidates.rationale: Scientifically real PR707/711 bugs, but package reproduction and unavailable MPI environment obscure capability hardness.

candidates.name: Amplitude-damping approximate code construction
candidates.rationale: Strong inverse-design potential, but reliable achievable thresholds require substantial additional encoder/recovery validation.

candidates.name: Noise-trajectory variance prediction
candidates.rationale: Can create held-out simulated outcomes, but distribution design and simulator throughput make it less trustworthy than active calibration.

candidates.name: Pauli-twirling falsification under correlated errors
candidates.rationale: Elementary coherent accumulation often gives an easy witness; a constrained task risks artificial exclusions.

candidates.name: Memory-constrained noisy adjoint differentiation
candidates.rationale: Useful but likely collapses to implementing a known adjoint/checkpointing algorithm rather than a research search gap.

candidates.name: Low-depth frustrated Hamiltonian ground-state design
candidates.rationale: Potentially hard, but feasibility and spectral-normalization choices are less transparent than directly supplied unitary targets.
